findings.text: hold_reason is the delivered decision but nothing consults it: a grep over reckon/, scripts/ and tests/ at the final head finds no importer of standing_suite outside its own test file, so a tier none or light promotion is not actually held by this code and the plan section's clause about a collection failure holding a tier-none promotion is true only at the module level. The reviewed manifest and the fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk/the-suite-is-declared-and-recorded.html:97 both disclose the wiring as separate work, so this is recorded as an open clause of the section rather than as a repair this run could have made.

item_verdicts.call_sites: no production call sites found - grep over reckon/, scripts/ and tests/ at the final head shows no importer of standing_suite outside tests/test_standing_suite.py, which is the disclosed deferral of the promotion wiring rather than an oversight.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 348688e8; the repair round changes _build_counts at reckon/crew/standing_suite.py:285 to an evidence-based rule, adds the guard tests at tests/test_standing_suite.py:122 and :146, reworks the budget case at :216, and leaves the module's imports and the declaration untouched; nothing in the diff reaches outside reckon/crew/standing_suite.py, tests/test_standing_suite.py and the evidence documents.
item_verdicts.done_when: both defects the first review named are repaired and re-measured at the final head - the collection rule now distinguishes a suite that ran and failed from one that never collected (review-logs/collection-rule-final.log against review-logs/collection-rule-old.log, where collected is null and both the failing and the xdist cases are recorded as collection failures), and the two-argument hold_reason raises StandingSuiteError on an unresolvable root instead of returning no hold, covered at tests/test_standing_suite.py:146; my own re-run of the gate at 493551e7 is 95 passed, 2 skipped, EXIT=0 and my own red arm at the same head fails exactly the named test (review-logs/head-arm-final.log, review-logs/red-arm-final.log); the follow-on list is disclosed rather than delivered - promotion wiring, the wave-close run, and the atomic-writer migration.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is a project-declared suite command and whole-run budget, a runner recording each run's counts at a named revision, and a hold for tier none and light; the three pieces land at reckon/crew/standing_suite.py:196, :336 and :402 over the declaration in docs/state/reckon/flight.yaml:96, and my own six-case measurement over a copy of the final head records the counts correctly in the declared form - collected=2, passed=1, failed=1, collection_failed=false for a -q -n 2 run over one passing and one failing test, collected=1, failed=1, false for a single-process -q failure, and a hold for exit 5 and for a syntax error (review-logs/collection-rule-final.log) - but hold_reason has no production caller, so the tier-none hold the goal names is a tested decision rather than an enforced one.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it carries the base arm at 348688e8 (85 passed, over the gate file that exists at base), the head arm at 468a24ba (95 passed, 2 skipped, over both gate files), the red negative control with its verbatim first line and EXIT=1, the borrowed-writer clause and the schema source as disclosed deviations, and the round-one repairs with their measurements; the added-failure derivation over the arms it names is 0 and [] by both the production function and my own parse (review-logs/added-failures.log), with a positive control over the run's own negative-control log finding the one canonical id.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the six commits touch exactly the nine declared paths and nothing else - a366947c the seven code, config and test paths, cd36faeb the fragment and the figure, and the later commits the repairs and the evidence - with reckon/schema/flight.yaml the one path beyond the assigned eight, disclosed and justified by the byte-parity tests that hold the generated pair to its LinkML source; the final commit is fragment-only and the amended commit's tree is unchanged from its predecessor, as the manifest states.

justifications.durability: the repaired rule is guarded by tests that fail under a mutation of the guarded function (measured: review-logs/red-arm-final.log) and the budget stop at tests/test_standing_suite.py:216 still proves the process group gone, but no test exercises the hold's over-budget-only sentence - my measurement shows a killed run also carries collection_failed, so that branch is read only in combination - and the record still depends on a private writer in another package at reckon/crew/standing_suite.py:476.
justifications.evidence: both gate arms are logged with revisions and digests and zero FAILED ids, the negative control's first line is the required string with EXIT=1, my own re-run at the final head is 95 passed, 2 skipped, EXIT=0, and my own red arm reproduces the failure the guard covers (review-logs/head-arm-final.log, review-logs/red-arm-final.log), with the added-failure count derived as 0 and [] by two parses and a positive control (review-logs/added-failures.log).
justifications.fit: the module reuses the repository's idioms (call-time imports, records under the project state tree) and adds no ruff finding over base, old or new under the declared config, but the call-time import of another package's private writer at reckon/crew/standing_suite.py:476 remains the round-one fit ding.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/standing_suite.py:196, :336 and :402 land the named pieces and the repaired counts now hold in the declared command form (review-logs/collection-rule-final.log), but hold_reason has no production caller, so the enforcement the goal names is not yet reachable outside the tests.
justifications.scope_discipline: the six commits touch exactly the nine declared paths, and the one beyond the assigned eight, reckon/schema/flight.yaml, is the LinkML source behind a generated pair the repository holds byte-identical, so it is disclosed and justified rather than silent.
